lines: Two chimneys smoking on the square. It almost looks like a town again.
You hear it? The lantern hums. Moss says the Ferns are on their way back from the halt farm.
Go and see her at the stall. If folk are coming home, she'll know what they need.
That's the light that fell? Put it in the lantern by the well. The old folk said that's what it was for.
The hatch by the stone circle is open now. Mind the thorns down there.
Whatever's sleeping on that shard isn't wicked. It's sick with the light. Free it, don't finish it.
Listen to that bellows! Ten years I've worked this fire and I've never been so glad to hear it.
Now, the light that fell. It came down inside the stone circle, and the circle's hollow underneath.
There's an old hatch by the stones. I've unbarred it for you. Bring the light back here, if you can lift it.
Slates from the roof came down across my door. Moss will sell you beams and nails for 30 Glint.
See the mark by the door? Clear it there and I can light the forge.
I need 30 Glint of beams and nails to clear my door, and I've nothing left.
The sign by the stones in the woodland had a pouch on it. Someone wanted those mosslings calmed.
That's my smithy. Was my smithy. The roof held, but the slates came down across the door.
Get me in there and I'll have the forge going by nightfall.
Talk to Moss at the stall first. She knows who's still here and who ran.
East along the path, then the garden walk down to the square. I'll take the short cut over the bank and meet you there.
Bramble! You're alive. I came out to see where the star fell and lost the path in the dark.
Half of Crossroads ran to the halt farm when the storm hit. Take the east path home. I know a short cut over the bank: I'll meet you on the square.
The Ferns are home, their beds are dug, and the stall has customers again. I'd forgotten the sound of that.
Go on, Ada's waiting by her door.
The Ferns' door is still under the rubble. Clear it at the mark, and I'll knock a little off the timber for you.
Look at the lantern! The smoke's stopped over the crater, too.
The Ferns sent word from the halt farm. They'll come home if there's a house to come home to.
Bramble. And Hale with you! I thought the woods had you both.
It's me and the stall, mostly. The well's choked, the bakery's cold, the Ferns are at the halt farm.
And there's a crater in the park that still smokes. Talk to Hale. If her forge burns, we can mend the rest.
Bramble! You're alive. Have you seen Hale?
She went out along the woodland's east path last night to see where the star fell, and she hasn't come back.
Stall's open. It's the only thing on the square that is.
The roof of my herbalist's is in the bakery's yard. When the Ferns are settled, help me put it on again.
Until then, nothing to brew with. Your terrace beds will change that.
Morel. I mix the tonics. Mixed. The storm put half my jars on the floor and the other half in the street.
Mind the mosslings in the woods. They aren't angry. The fallen light has got into them, like a fever.
We'll dig your beds over in the morning. The least we can do.
Our door! We slept in a hay loft for a week.
Thank you, Bramble. When the beds are dug, come and see what grows.
We saw the lantern from the halt farm road. But the door's still buried.
A fresh note in Moss's hand: WATER IN THE WELL. APOTHECARY OPEN. THE FERNS ARE HOME.
Under it: COL PATH TO THE FROSTLINE STILL BURIED. HALT ROAD SHUT. WORD HERE WHEN THEY OPEN.
A note in Moss's hand: THE FERNS ARE HOME. THE WELL IS STILL CHOKED AND THE HERBALIST'S ROOF IS STILL OFF. ASK AT THE STALL, OR ASK MOREL.
A new note: THE LANTERN IS LIT. THE FERNS ARE COMING HOME. A HAND WITH THEIR DOOR WOULD BE KIND.
Torn notices. One survives: MARKET DAY, SATURDAY. The rest the storm took.
The waystone is cracked through. It will carry travellers again once the valley's ways are mended.
The great shard hums in the lantern. One of many, by the look of the empty cradles.
You lift the shard into the lantern's cradle. Light runs down the iron and into the well.
An iron lantern beside the well, older than the town, with a dozen empty cradles.
Your hut came through the storm, roof and all. The door is swollen shut with the rain. It can wait: the square needs you more than your bed does.
The forge is lit.
You pay 30 Glint for beams and nails and clear the slates from the door. Hale's fire takes on the first try.
Slates and beams block the smithy door. Clearing it needs 30 Glint of timber.
The door is clear.
You pay 20 Glint for timber and clear the rubble from the Ferns' door. The shutters open.
Rubble blocks the Ferns' door. Clearing it needs 20 Glint of timber.
